name: @kolu/acp-harness
//exports: ONE door, and it is one on purpose: a second subpath would be a second way to reach a subprocess, and there is exactly one subprocess. What the door now hands out beside `startHarness` is the conversation layer itself — `Transcript`, `Turns`, the held list, and the `says`/`plus` rules over a change — because two products run one conversation each and both must be served by the same classes rather than by a copy in each.
//scripts: `test:daemon`, not `test:unit`: almost every test here spawns a real ACP agent as a detached process group (the fixture agents `@kolu/acp-client/testlib` hands out), which is the lane `just test-daemon` runs serially and `just test-unit` skips — the same reason `kolu-omp` declares it. A package declares ONE lane, so the pure `src/noProductImports.test.ts` rides along in it.
//dependencies: `@kolu/acp-client` RUNS THE PROTOCOL — this package holds one conversation on top of it and spawns nothing itself, so the SDK is the client's runtime dependency and no longer this one's (`packages/acp/src/manifest.test.ts` holds that). `effect` is a runtime dependency for the same reason: the client's verbs are Effects, and the one boundary in `conversation.ts` runs them. NO PRODUCT PACKAGE, and that is the shape of this door: the rows and the state are the product's own, declared in the product's tree and reached here only through the type a caller instantiates this package with (`src/noProductImports.test.ts` holds it red). The versions are LITERAL rather than `catalog:` because olai vendors this directory and installs its manifest from its own workspace, where kolu's catalog does not exist.
//devDependencies: Nothing but the toolchain: the fixture agents this suite spawns are `@kolu/acp-client`'s, and the client is a runtime dependency above.
